Prepared Dried Yak Cheese (Chhurpi)

Served at: Losar (Tibetan New Year)

Makes about 1 cup (240 ml) of softened chhurpi piecesPrep 4 hours (soaking)Cook 10 min (optional pan-frying)

Dried yak cheese, known as chhurpi, is a staple snack in Tibetan culture, often enjoyed during celebrations like Losar, the Tibetan New Year. Its unique hard texture and savory, tangy flavor make it a distinctive treat. This preparation method makes the chhurpi more approachable for those new to it, softening it slightly for easier enjoyment as a festive snack.

Ingredients

  • 100 g (about 3.5 oz) hard dried yak cheese (chhurpi)
  • 2 cups (470 ml) warm water, plus more for rinsing
  • Optional: 1/4 teaspoon chili powder
  • Optional: 1/8 teaspoon salt

Method

  1. Rinse the dried yak cheese pieces thoroughly under cold running water to remove any surface dust or impurities.
  2. Place the rinsed chhurpi in a bowl and cover with 2 cups (470 ml) of warm water. Let it soak for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, until the cheese softens slightly. The longer it soaks, the softer it will become.
  3. Once softened, drain the water. If the chhurpi pieces are large, you can carefully cut them into smaller, bite-sized pieces using a sharp knife.
  4. For a chewier texture, you can serve the softened chhurpi as is.
  5. Alternatively, for a slightly crispy exterior and enhanced flavor, heat a dry skillet over medium heat. Add the softened chhurpi pieces and cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they are lightly browned and slightly chewy.
  6. If desired, sprinkle with chili powder and salt during the last minute of cooking, tossing to coat evenly.
  7. Serve warm or at room temperature as a unique snack.

Tips

  • Adjust soaking time to your preference; longer soaking results in a softer chew.
  • Chhurpi can also be added to soups or stews for a tangy, cheesy flavor.
  • Store any leftover softened chhurpi in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.
